claims.text: High-stress sliding wear can produce an in-situ nanocrystalline surface layer in high-entropy-alloy coatings.
Formation of the nanocrystalline surface layer governs enhanced wear resistance.
The nanocrystalline surface layer increases surface hardness.
The nanocrystalline surface layer impedes wear-related damage mechanisms.
A post-deposition anneal can coarsen the near-surface grains of the coating.
Anneal-induced near-surface grain coarsening will inhibit or reduce formation of the wear-induced nanocrystalline layer.
Severe plastic deformation during high-stress sliding causes rapid surface grain refinement.
The resulting nanocrystalline layer resists dislocation motion.
The resulting nanocrystalline layer resists crack initiation.
As-deposited coatings that form a robust nanocrystalline surface layer will have lower wear rates than pre-annealed coatings in which layer formation is suppressed.
As-deposited coatings naturally form the nanocrystalline layer during wear testing.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold when wear is dominated by severe plastic deformation under high contact stress.
The proposed relationship may not hold when chemical effects dominate wear.
The proposed relationship may not hold when high-temperature effects dominate wear.
The quantitative difference in wear rate between as-deposited and annealed coatings is not specified and remains uncertain.
